source.title: Defensive Unlearning with Adversarial Training for Robust Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
source.authors: Yimeng Zhang; Xin Chen; Jing-Han Jia; Yihua Zhang; Chong-Yu Fan; Jiancheng Liu; Mingyi Hong; Ke Ding; Si-Jia Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adversarial prompt attacks recover erased concepts in diffusion models and whether adversarial-training-based unlearning reduces that recovery. This is a different model type and evaluation setting from the claim’s LLM examples.
record.gate_note: The study reports attack success rates (ASR) for adversarial prompts that cause diffusion models to generate the concept targeted for erasure. It does not test recovery through fine-tuning on small unrelated sets, activation-direction ablation, weight quantization, or non-adversarial prompt rephrasing. ASR is not a measurement of un-attacked targeted-knowledge accuracy or of near-chance performance before an attack.
record.test_reason: Applies the shallow-unlearning question to text-to-image diffusion models. It measures how often adversarial prompts regenerate erased concepts (nudity, Van Gogh style, objects) in models unlearned with ESD, FMN, UCE, SPM, AC, SalUn, ED and SH. This bears on E. It also proposes AdvUnlearn, an adversarial-training method claimed to resist these prompt attacks, which bears on F. The system type differs from the LLM originals; see notes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that current unlearned DMs remain vulnerable to adversarial prompt attacks. AdvUnlearn, which uses adversarial training with a utility-retaining regularizer on the text encoder, improves robustness while largely preserving utility, and its encoder transfers plug-and-play to other DMs. They note computational cost as a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: Adversarial-training-based concept erasure for diffusion models: optimizes a text encoder using adversarial prompt generation, an ESD-style erasure objective, and a retain-prompt utility regularizer; not an LLM unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack method (including CCE versus discrete prompt attacks), model type for transferred text encoders, optimized module (text encoder versus UNet), encoder depth, retain-set source and filtering, regularization weight, and adversarial training steps affect reported outcomes.
record.problems: The reported attack success rates do not establish the un-attacked concept-generation rate or show that target performance was near chance before the attack. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The main base-model experiments use SD v1.4; the paper evaluates other diffusion models through transferred encoders but does not test the LLM-specific recovery routes in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Table A5’s comparator-model ASRs for P4D are not separately listed; the corresponding models’ main UnlearnDiffAtk results are in Tables 5–7, and the additional AdvUnlearn P4D result is r59. Table A1 repeats nudity-unlearning results also shown in Table 5. Utility measures (FID and CLIP) are not included because they do not measure recovery of the erased concept.

untested.parts: No no-attack concept-generation rate for the unlearned models is reported, so near-chance erasure before attack is not shown. The authors only state that unlearned models do well on non-adversarial prompts.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
Only optimized adversarial prompts and embedding attacks (UnlearnDiffAtk, CCE, PEZ, PH2P, P4D) are tested. Plain rephrasing, other languages and in-context information are not.
AdvUnlearn's resistance to fine-tuning, internal edits or quantization is not tested.

missing.what: CCE/PEZ/PH2P ASRs for AdvUnlearn on Van Gogh, Church, Parachute, Tench and Garbage Truck. CCE gives 28%, 36%, 48%, 24% and 44%.
SH and ED nudity ASRs (7.04%, 2.11%) with FIDs of 128.53 and 233.31. These are not in Table 5, contrary to rows_left_out.
P4D ASRs for comparators (FMN 97.89%, SPM 91.55%, UCE 75.35%, ESD 71.27%, SalUn 12.68%)

Design dependence of AdvUnlearn: AT-ESD on UNet 43.48%, AdvUnlearn on UNet 64.79%, fast AT 28.87%, one encoder layer 72.54%, regularization weight 13.18–36.63%, ImageNet unfiltered retain set 51.41%, Replace/Add prompting 36.63%/45.07%.
missing.locator: Tables 1–4, A3, A4; Fig. 8, Fig. A3

record.verdict_notes: All reader version ids (V5/V6) were invalid and are remapped to E/F. The study is on text-to-image diffusion models rather than the LLMs of the original sources, so it is classed T3 (new setting). Researchers may judge that a concept-generation ASR is a different construct from LLM knowledge recovery. No no-attack ASR for unlearned models is given, so recovery cannot be measured against a post-unlearning baseline. No uncertainty is reported. The default test attack UnlearnDiffAtk comes from the same group.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report targeted-concept performance on ordinary prompts before attack, so it does not establish that unlearning first brought that performance near chance; nor does it test general ability as stated in this version.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.

Tests adversarial prompt attacks on text-to-image diffusion models, not other languages or in-context information; it does not test ordinary rephrasing without an adversarial prompt-generation procedure.
Tests AdvUnlearn against the reported prompt attacks; does not test resistance to fine-tuning, activation edits, or quantization.

relation.reason: It measures adversarial-prompt regeneration of erased concepts across eight erasure methods and its own method.

tranche.reason: A new setting (text-to-image diffusion concept erasure) with attack results bearing on E and F. The reader's T2 is less apt.

source_check.notes: SD v1.4 image-concept erasure, not LLM knowledge. ASR is judged by classifiers (NudeNet, WikiArt ViT, ResNet-50). Base SD is 100%, and the paper gives no no-attack ASR for the unlearned models. P4D shares AdvUnlearn's training loss. l0's reason takes '24%' from SH Parachute. l3's 'dissimilar DMs' includes SD v1.5 (r26), which the paper calls similar. l3 cites r24 and r31, which are not in this pack.

statements.correction: Under UnlearnDiffAtk on SD v1.4, FMN, SPM, UCE, AC and ESD give 26-100% ASR (lowest: ESD Garbage Truck 26%). ESD nudity is 73.24%. FMN is 100% on Garbage Truck, Parachute and Tench and 96% on Church.
statements.problem: For FMN, SPM, UCE, AC and ESD the low end is 26%, not 24%. The 24% is SH on Parachute, a method the statement doesn't name. 'FMN objects 100%' leaves out FMN Church at 96%.

statements.correction: AdvUnlearn nudity ASR on SD v1.4: 21.13% under UnlearnDiffAtk (ESD 73.24%, FMN 97.89%) and 39.44% under CCE. With the transferred encoder, DreamShaper is 61.27%, against 90.14% with its original encoder. Resistance is incomplete, not absent.
statements.problem: The AdvUnlearn numbers are right, but they sit under 'challenges' with no comparators. In this study AdvUnlearn's resistance is reduced, not absent: its verdict is l3 limits_scope.
